q: For Miss Tibbs was merely the daughter of the hotel-keeper; and although Tibbs was a Southerner, and had owned "his own <DW65>s" in the States, she was of inferior position and a protegee of Cissy's.

l: From Sand Hill to Pine, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
s: Yuba Bill stops the stagecoach after a fallen tree blocks the road near the site of a robbery six months earlier. While Bill and several passengers work on clearing the road, other members of the coach party take shelter in a cabin occupied by Hiram, Sophy, and Flo, the niece of Snapshot Harry, the alleged coach robber. Flo’s bold humor eases the tension caused by the family’s resentment of investigators and travelers. After the road is cleared, the passengers return to the coach, while the quiet, observant passenger and the box-seat occupant are said to have joined the clearing party.

l: Yuba Bill, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
s: Yuba Bill, the stagecoach driver, stops the coach when a fallen tree blocks the road and orders the stranger to bring a large wood axe. He is impatient with the passengers and the cabin’s occupants, but leads the road-clearing effort and returns after the obstruction is removed.

l: Ned Brice, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
s: Ned Brice is the expressman traveling with the coach and initially reports that a tree has fallen across the road. He remains concerned about his duty and the key to the treasure compartment, accompanies the passengers to the cabin, and defends Yuba Bill’s roughness by mentioning the recent robbery.

l: Frank Frenshaw, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
s: Frank Frenshaw, editor of the Mountain Banner, offers to accompany the lady to the cabin and joins the other passengers there. He tries to suggest explanations for the family’s persecution but is interrupted by Flo’s laughter.

l: Heckshill, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
s: Sam Heckshill of Heckshill & Dobbs’s Flour Mills introduces the passengers at the cabin and uses a light, noncommittal philosophy to ease the awkward situation. He reaches for the whiskey and competes with Frenshaw for Flo’s attention.

l: Snapshot Harry, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
s: Snapshot Harry is identified as the man who stopped the coach six months earlier. Flo is said to be his niece, and she jokes that he will hold up the next Pioneer Coach to make enough money to send her to Europe.

l: Flora Dimwood, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
s: Flo is Snapshot Harry’s niece and a young woman with an audacious, attractive manner. She openly acknowledges her uncle’s identity, defends Hiram and Sophy against the stage company’s treatment, serves whiskey and coffee to the passengers, and playfully unsettles the expressman.

l: Hiram Tarbox, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
s: Hiram is one of the cabin’s occupants and is treated as an old cousin by Flo. He and Sophy have endured visits from constables, detectives, newspaper men, and other strangers because of their connection to Snapshot Harry, and he helps receive the passengers with an apathetic manner.

l: Mrs. Tarbox, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
s: Sophy is Hiram’s wife or close household companion and helps prepare coffee in the cabin. She complains that the stage company’s suspicion and persecution have made life difficult, while affectionately rebuking Flo for being a discredit and bother.

l: the quiet, observant passenger, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
s: The quiet, observant passenger reassures the lady that there is no immediate danger and criticizes the expressman indirectly for leaving his post. He refuses to go to the cabin at first, but is later reported to have joined the road-clearing party.

l: the coach party, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
s: The coach party is awakened when the stagecoach stops and becomes uneasy after learning that the obstruction is near the site of a former robbery. Several passengers shelter in the cabin, where Flo’s humor breaks the tension, and they later return hurriedly to the coach without questioning Yuba Bill as planned.

l: the stagecoach, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
s: The stagecoach is halted on a rainy night by a fallen tree across the road. It is near the location where the up coach was robbed six months earlier, and it resumes its journey after the passengers and road workers clear the obstruction.

l: the stage road, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
s: The road is obstructed by a fallen tree near a cabin and a former coach-robbery site. Yuba Bill and several helpers work to clear it, while the stranger warns that the coach might otherwise have gone down a canyon.

l: uncle Hiram's cabin, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
s: The cabin is an unpainted, four-roomed redwood structure with a fire but little other comfort or light. Hiram, Sophy, and Flo shelter the visiting passengers there with coffee and whiskey while the road is being cleared.

l: tree obstruction, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
s: The fallen tree lies across the road and forces the stagecoach to stop. Yuba Bill considers the coach’s regulation axe ineffective, obtains a larger axe and ropes, and leads the effort to remove the tree.

l: the coach robbery, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
s: The coach robbery occurred six months earlier less than a hundred yards from the cabin. The event caused continuing suspicion and official and public attention toward Hiram and Sophy because of their association with Snapshot Harry.

l: the road-clearing, From Sand Hill to Pine, BILSON'S HOUSEKEEPER FROM SAND HILL TO PINE A NIECE OF SNAPSHOT HARRY'S I There was a slight jarring though the whole frame of the coach, a grinding and hissing from the brakes, and then a sudden jolt as the vehicle ran upon and recoiled from the taut pole-straps of the now arrested horses.
s: The road-clearing is organized by Yuba Bill, who calls for passengers and the stranger to bring proper tools and help. Several outside passengers assist, and the quiet, observant passenger and the box-seat occupant are later said to have joined them.

l: From Sand Hill to Pine, From Sand Hill to Pine, Five minutes after Bill had gathered up the reins, they reached the scene of obs
s: Yuba Bill's coach is stopped by a masked horseman and armed accomplices, who take the express box during a stage robbery. Brice discovers that the treasure, a packet of greenbacks, had already been removed from the box, apparently while he was away at a settler's cabin. Bill believes the thieves were sneaks or traitors among the passengers rather than Snapshot Harry, who would likely pursue them after discovering the deception. Brice decides to seek out Snapshot Harry, while Bill promises to protect him in his report to the company.

l: Yuba Bill, From Sand Hill to Pine, Five minutes after Bill had gathered up the reins, they reached the scene of obs
s: Yuba Bill guides the coach through the obstructed road and stops when a masked horseman orders him to halt. He prevents the expressman from using his rifle, has him surrender the express box, and later urges Brice to remain calm. Bill believes Snapshot Harry was not involved in the theft of the treasure and suggests that sneaks or traitors among the passengers took it.

l: Brice, From Sand Hill to Pine, Five minutes after Bill had gathered up the reins, they reached the scene of obs
s: Brice, the expressman, prepares to defend the express box but obeys Yuba Bill's command to hand it down. He discovers that the lock has been forced and the packet of greenbacks is already missing, then tells Bill that he believes the money was taken while he was at the settler's cabin. After hearing about Snapshot Harry, Brice decides to find him.

l: Snapshot Harry, From Sand Hill to Pine, Five minutes after Bill had gathered up the reins, they reached the scene of obs
s: Snapshot Harry leads or is associated with the gang that stops the coach, but Bill insists that Harry did not arrange the tree obstruction or participate in the underhand theft. Bill expects Harry to discover that his gang has deceived him and pursue the thieves. He says Harry is more than half white, lives somewhere near a cabin in the bush, and has a crippled sister and her daughter.

l: Ned Brice, From Sand Hill to Pine, Five minutes after Bill had gathered up the reins, they reached the scene of obs
s: The expressman reaches for his rifle when the coach is stopped, but Yuba Bill restrains him because the attackers have them covered. He hands the express box to one of the masked figures after finding that its lock has been forced and its packet of greenbacks removed.

l: the gang, From Sand Hill to Pine, Five minutes after Bill had gathered up the reins, they reached the scene of obs
s: The robbers stop the coach with a fallen tree, cover the passengers with hidden guns, and take the express box. The text suggests that other robbers or traitors had already removed the treasure before the main group stopped the coach.

l: Snapshot Harry's gang, From Sand Hill to Pine, Five minutes after Bill had gathered up the reins, they reached the scene of obs
s: Snapshot Harry's gang is scattered for miles after the robbery, and a posse is sent down the road in pursuit of Harry. Bill suspects that two sneaks or traitors who traveled as passengers may have taken the treasure without Harry's knowledge.

l: the stagecoach, From Sand Hill to Pine, Five minutes after Bill had gathered up the reins, they reached the scene of obs
s: The coach passes through a narrow opening between sections of a fallen pine tree before being halted by masked robbers. After the express box is taken, Yuba Bill drives it furiously for three miles to the first station, where it later departs with the passengers.

l: express box, From Sand Hill to Pine, Five minutes after Bill had gathered up the reins, they reached the scene of obs
s: The express box is surrendered to the robbers during the stage robbery. Brice has found that its lock was forced and manages to snap it shut again before handing it down, concealing that the treasure is already gone.

l: the recovered treasure, From Sand Hill to Pine, Five minutes after Bill had gathered up the reins, they reached the scene of obs
s: The treasure is a packet of greenbacks that was missing from the express box before the robbers took it. Brice believes it was removed while he was away at the settler's cabin, leaving the robbers with an empty box.

l: Tarbox's cabin, From Sand Hill to Pine, Five minutes after Bill had gathered up the reins, they reached the scene of obs
s: Brice had left the coach and gone to a settler's cabin before the robbery. He believes the treasure was taken during his absence.

l: the stage robbery, From Sand Hill to Pine, Five minutes after Bill had gathered up the reins, they reached the scene of obs
s: The stage robbery involves masked and armed men stopping Yuba Bill's coach, taking the express box, and allowing the coach to continue. The robbery is later revealed to have been preceded by the theft of the treasure from inside the box, possibly by passengers connected with the gang.

l: From Sand Hill to Pine, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
s: Mr. Ned Brice visits Hiram Tarbox and his wife, using a flattering newspaper account of the robbery to gain their cooperation and learn how to reach Flora Tarbox and Snapshot Harry's secluded home. Brice follows a narrow mountain trail marked at times by Flora's footprints, crossing the ridge and the North Fork canyon into an isolated hollow. Near the hollow, an unidentified rifleman shoots Brice's hat, dispatch bag, and handkerchief without killing him. The rifleman then approaches, recognizes Brice as the expressman, and offers him whiskey at a cabin while Brice says he wants to see Snapshot Harry.

l: Brice, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
s: Mr. Ned Brice brings Hiram Tarbox a copy of the Red Dog Clarion containing praise for Hiram's assistance during the robbery, then asks for directions to Flora Tarbox. He follows the mountain trail toward Snapshot Harry's home, survives several deliberately aimed rifle shots, and continues toward the shooter. He tells the shooter that he wants to see Snapshot Harry.

l: Yuba Bill, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
s: Yuba Bill is praised in the local press for his well-known coolness during the robbery. The newspaper account also says that Hiram Tarbox timely warned him about the obstruction.

l: Hiram Tarbox, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
s: Hiram Tarbox is delighted to read a newspaper account naming him as an esquire who helped remove the obstruction and provided hospitality to delayed passengers. He gives Brice directions to the hidden trail leading toward Harry's home, while warning him to look out for himself.

l: Flora Dimwood, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
s: Flora Tarbox has left the Tarbox cabin at sun-up and gone to her uncle's home. Her footprints mark parts of the difficult trail Brice follows, and Hiram's wife says Flora sometimes wanders outside the hollow when she becomes lonesome.

l: Snapshot Harry, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
s: Snapshot Harry lives in a secluded valley or hollow reached by a concealed trail from the road. Hiram says Harry visits the Tarbox cabin only on nights when the coach is not running and there is no travel. Brice travels toward the hollow intending to see him.

l: the stagecoach, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
s: The stagecoach was delayed by the tree obstruction and was then robbed. The newspaper account claims that, without Hiram Tarbox's warning to Yuba Bill, it might have crashed into the tree.

l: the stage road, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
s: The road passes the place where the tree was thrown down and runs along a mountain shelf above the North Fork canyon. A narrow trail parallels part of it while remaining hidden by thorn and brush, and the stage road eventually crosses the canyon on a high bridge.

l: obstruction site, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
s: The obstruction site is where the tree blocked the road and where the trail up the mountain begins. Brice uses this location to find the concealed route described by Hiram Tarbox.

l: the narrow mountain trail, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
s: The mountain trail is less than a foot wide in places and remains hidden from the road by brush while providing a view of the road below. It climbs to a ridge, descends through a wilder area, and ultimately leads toward the North Fork canyon and Harry's hollow.

l: North Fork, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
s: The North Fork flows through a canyon below the stage road and then turns along the mountain side. Brice follows a faint ledge beside its current while using Flora's footprint as a guide.

l: North Fork canyon, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
s: The North Fork canyon is enclosed by narrow, precipitous walls, with the stage road and its bridge hundreds of feet above. Brice reaches the canyon, crosses along a faint ledge formed by driftwood and cliff debris, and emerges near the isolated hollow.

l: outlaw's hollow, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
s: The outlaw's hollow is a small, secluded valley enclosed by surrounding heights and little buckeye-covered hills. It is inaccessible from the stage road's side because of a sheer cliff and is protected by difficult approaches.

l: tree obstruction, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
s: The tree obstruction was thrown across the road and was described in the newspaper as possibly the preliminary work of the robber gang. It was removed with Hiram Tarbox's assistance, and its location helps Brice find the mountain trail.

l: the stage robbery, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
s: The robbery receives extensive praise-filled coverage in the local press, including commendations of Yuba Bill, the young expressman, the passengers, and a lady passenger. The article also calls for a Vigilance Committee, though local readers apparently think the wealthy express companies can protect their own property.

l: shooting at Mr. Ned Brice, From Sand Hill to Pine, II The robbery furnished the usual amount of copy for the local press.
s: An unseen marksman fires at Mr. Ned Brice near the hollow, piercing his hat, shooting through his dispatch bag, and tearing his handkerchief from his fingers. Brice realizes the shooter is under a sycamore and walks toward him; the marksman then emerges alive and treats the encounter as a test of Brice's courage.

l: From Sand Hill to Pine, From Sand Hill to Pine, When Brice had partaken of the whiskey, the stranger, who had kept silence, poin
s: Brice tells Henry Dimwood, alias Snapshot Harry, that he knew the coach's lock had been forced and accepts blame for failing to warn anyone. Henry explains that two men from the gang secretly robbed the coach before the gang stopped it, making Yuba Bill and the coach victims of two robberies in one evening. Brice proposes recovering the greenbacks and turning the thief over to the express company, but Henry must consult his gang before agreeing. Henry sends Flora with Brice as a guide, and the two discuss their growing familiarity while traveling away from the gang's hideout.

l: Brice, From Sand Hill to Pine, When Brice had partaken of the whiskey, the stranger, who had kept silence, poin
s: Brice tells Henry Dimwood that he knew the coach's lock had been forced when he handed down the box, but snapped it together again and accepted sole blame. He proposes working with Henry to recover the greenbacks and later travels with Flora, whose company protects him from questioning by the gang.

l: Snapshot Harry, From Sand Hill to Pine, When Brice had partaken of the whiskey, the stranger, who had kept silence, poin
s: Henry Dimwood, also known as Snapshot Harry, explains the circumstances of the two robberies and says the thief is trapped along the road. He listens to Brice's recovery plan, agrees to sound out the gang, and sends Flora to guide Brice safely away.

l: Flora Dimwood, From Sand Hill to Pine, When Brice had partaken of the whiskey, the stranger, who had kept silence, poin
s: Flora accompanies Brice as his guide and protection from the gang's questions. She jokes and flirts with him, gives him her handkerchief while offering to mend his, and reveals that Henry is protective of her because of his outlaw reputation.

l: Yuba Bill, From Sand Hill to Pine, When Brice had partaken of the whiskey, the stranger, who had kept silence, poin
s: Yuba Bill did not know about the first robbery when it occurred, but Brice told him at the station. Henry takes pleasure in the fact that Yuba Bill and his coach were robbed twice in one evening.

l: the gang, From Sand Hill to Pine, When Brice had partaken of the whiskey, the stranger, who had kept silence, poin
s: The gang includes about twenty-five men, each of whom has a share in the greenbacks. Two gang members secretly arranged the first robbery, while the rest later stopped the coach without knowing that those two had betrayed them.

l: the express company, From Sand Hill to Pine, When Brice had partaken of the whiskey, the stranger, who had kept silence, poin
s: Brice proposes that the express company be told that the stealthy introduction of robbers as passengers was not Henry's method. He suggests that recovering the greenbacks and delivering the thief to the company could earn a reward and its good opinion.

l: Tarbox's cabin, From Sand Hill to Pine, When Brice had partaken of the whiskey, the stranger, who had kept silence, poin
s: Tarbox's cabin is connected with the events surrounding the robbery because the two conspirators got a scout to cut down the tree by falsely claiming it was part of Henry's orders. The road from Tarbox's cabin to the bridge remains watched by Henry's men, trapping the escaped thief.

l: the stagecoach, From Sand Hill to Pine, When Brice had partaken of the whiskey, the stranger, who had kept silence, poin
s: The coach carried the greenbacks and was first robbed by two men who had taken seats as passengers. Henry's gang then stopped the coach as well, causing it to be robbed twice within half an hour.

l: the recovered treasure, From Sand Hill to Pine, When Brice had partaken of the whiskey, the stranger, who had kept silence, poin
s: The greenbacks were secretly taken from the coach before Henry's gang stopped it. The escaped thief still has them and is believed to be trapped on the watched road.
